featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Praguu JC
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently visited this small restaurant and was truly impressed. The food quality is excellent, and every dish tastes delicious and fresh. I also tried their fish, which was perfectly cooked and full of flavor. It’s definitely a place everyone must try! Highly recommended for great taste and freshness.

featured_reviews.name: Sunil D'Silva
featured_reviews.review_text: This is a small cosy village old-school home converted into a live kitchen which serves simply yet delicious seafood at a very nominal cost. The ladies who run the place are very kind and will answer all your questions peacefully while they are busy cooking. They serve mainly pomfret, bombil, tarli, ravas, manli and prawns fry and also ambotik and other fish curries. They also serve Chicken kheema and chicken curry and a few local vegetables. These can be accompanied by their famous rice bhakari or chapatis all made in-house. A must visit to pick food or even eat at the place if your looking for authentic village yummy food.

featured_reviews.name: Brad Dsouza
featured_reviews.review_text: Great home cooked food. Great hospitality. Out door seating lends to a very nice atmosphere. Affordable prices. Bring your appetite. The road is narrow but there's place to park 2-3 cars and a couple of bikes. Food is prepared in advance and laid out so you can see what you want and ask for it. It seems like certain items sell out quickly. Fried fish, chapati, hand bread are made fresh.

review_photos.caption: Chicken liver, vajri curry, fried bombil

featured_reviews.name: Mario Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: Good 'home made' food served with love and smile. Visit the place if you are in Gorai. Stella Aunty is very friendly and makes some good fare especially if it's seafood. The food is fresh and tasty. Ordered Mandeli, chicken curry and bombil fry. All was really good to taste.

featured_reviews.name: Wilfred Chettiar
featured_reviews.review_text: We visited the place after checking the reviews online. It was the best decision we made. It is a small place but Stella aunty is full of life. She welcomes each and every customer and treats them so well. The quality of food is awesome. Seafood is so so fresh and yummy. We ordered Prawns Curry, Prawns Fry, Pompret Fry and Misal Pav along with bhakri. The cost of all this was Rs. 750 which is very reasonable. Best place to have homely food and Stella aunty has lot of non veg variety. Will surely visit again.

featured_reviews.name: Omkar Udmale
featured_reviews.review_text:
First, let’s talk about the food. The sandwiches were incredibly fresh and flavorful. The bread was soft yet perfectly toasted, and the fillings were generous and well-seasoned. Every bite was satisfying, and you could really taste the quality of the ingredients. Whether you like classic combinations or something a bit more loaded, they have options that will definitely hit the spot.

The pizza was equally impressive. The crust had that perfect balance—crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. The sauce was rich and not overly sweet, and the cheese was melted to perfection. The toppings were fresh and plentiful, making each slice absolutely delicious. It’s the kind of pizza that keeps you reaching for “just one more slice.”

And the milkshakes—wow! Thick, creamy, and full of flavor. They were perfectly blended, not too sweet, and served chilled just right. It felt like the perfect finishing touch to an already amazing meal. The portion size was generous, and the presentation was great too.

The atmosphere of the restaurant was clean, comfortable, and welcoming. The staff were friendly, attentive, and quick with service. They made sure everything was served fresh and were happy to help with recommendations. It’s the kind of place where you can relax and enjoy your meal with friends or family.

Overall, this restaurant delivers great quality food, excellent service, and a cozy environment. I’ll definitely be coming back again and would highly recommend it to anyone craving delicious sandwiches, tasty pizza, and refreshing milkshakes!

featured_reviews.name: Shubham Mathkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Let’s talk about the food first. Overall, the experience was okayish. The menu has a wide variety of options, which is definitely a plus, but unfortunately the taste didn’t quite live up to expectations.
We started with the Manchow Soup, and honestly, this was the highlight of the meal. The flavour was good, comforting, and well-balanced. The portion size was decent for the price, making it a value-for-money starter.
Next, we tried the Honey Coriander Chicken. The dish was average—for ₹300, we received six pieces of chicken, which felt a little less. It leaned more towards the sweet side, though the server had already informed us that it would be sweet with a hint of spice, so there were no surprises there.
After that came the Chicken Shanghai Rice. While the portion size was generous, the dish itself was quite disappointing. The chicken quantity was minimal, with more egg and paneer dominating the rice. The rice was dry and lacked flavour, which really took away from the overall experience.
On a positive note, the ambience of the restaurant was really nice. There’s also an open seating area, which adds to the vibe and makes it a pleasant place to sit and relax. The staff was courteous and helpful, patiently explaining the dishes when needed.
To sum it up, the restaurant scores well on ambience and service, but the food quality needs improvement. Overall, I’d rate this place 2 out of 5.

Only downside is the service~ They are not the Top ones at suggesting items and the order takes in almost 25 minutes to be served especially on rush hours sunday nights.
Nevertheless a must visit in the area..

featured_reviews.name: santosh kumar Behera
featured_reviews.review_text:
Rai Gaon Market is a bustling hub that encapsulates the vibrant essence of a traditional market with a touch of modern convenience. From the moment you step into its lively atmosphere, you are greeted by an array of colors, sounds, and aromas that create an immersive shopping experience.

The market's diverse range of vendors offers everything from fresh produce to unique handmade crafts. The fruit and vegetable stalls boast a kaleidoscope of seasonal offerings, ensuring that you can always find the freshest ingredients for your culinary adventures. The local artisans showcase their talent through intricately designed handicrafts, providing a perfect blend of tradition and innovation.

What sets Rai Gaon Market apart is not just the variety of goods but also the warmth of its vendors. The sellers are not merely merchants; they are storytellers, sharing the history and significance behind their products. Engaging with them adds a personal touch to the shopping experience, turning it into a cultural exploration.

The market's layout is well-organized, making navigation easy for visitors. Clear signages and designated areas for different types of products contribute to a seamless shopping journey. Additionally, the incorporation of modern amenities, such as digital payment options and eco-friendly packaging choices, enhances the overall convenience for shoppers.

Food enthusiasts will find Rai Gaon Market to be a gastronomic delight. Local eateries offer an array of street food delicacies, providing a perfect opportunity to savor authentic flavors. Whether you crave savory snacks or have a sweet tooth, the market has something to satisfy every palate.

In conclusion, Rai Gaon Market is more than just a marketplace;
